title: Machine learning assists a proved dimension bound for affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties
summary: The authors used computational data and machine-learning pattern exploration to study affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties. They report rediscovering the previously known virtual-dimension formula, then using the exploration to formulate and prove a new lower bound on actual dimension. The mathematical theorem, not model accuracy or rediscovery of the known formula, is the specific result. The 2024 journal article and 2023 arXiv v1 are versions of one study.
ai_technology: Linear models, support-vector machines and neural networks
organization: Beijing International Center for Mathematical Research, Peking University; Center for Machine Learning Research, Peking University; University of Hong Kong

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full text and primary journal indexed full text, including methods, theorem, affiliations and version dates.

evidence.tested: The paper reports mathematical proof of a lower bound prompted by machine-learning exploration.
evidence.unknown: The virtual-dimension formula was previously known and is not the new theorem; the work is not a formal automated proof.
evidence.ai_role: Models explored generated mathematical data and highlighted patterns that led mathematicians to formulate and prove a new lower bound.
